name: Food and Diet
blurb: Dinh dưỡng, ăn uống, sản xuất thực phẩm

words.definitionEn: the process of providing or obtaining the food necessary for health and growth
words.example: Good nutrition is essential for maintaining a healthy immune system.

words.definitionEn: lack of proper nutrition, caused by not having enough to eat or not eating enough of the right foods
words.example: Malnutrition is a serious problem in many developing countries.

words.definitionEn: a unit of energy used to measure the energy content of food
words.example: A typical adult needs about 2000 calories per day to maintain weight.

words.definitionEn: a type of nutrient (such as carbohydrate, protein, or fat) that the body needs in large amounts
words.example: Carbohydrates, proteins, and fats are the three main macronutrients.

words.definitionEn: a nutrient such as a vitamin or mineral that the body needs in very small amounts
words.example: Micronutrient deficiencies can lead to various health problems.

words.definitionEn: a nutrient found in foods such as bread, rice, and pasta that provides energy
words.example: Complex carbohydrates like whole grains are healthier than simple sugars.

words.definitionEn: a nutrient essential for building and repairing body tissues
words.example: Lean meat, fish, and legumes are excellent sources of protein.

words.definitionEn: a nutrient that provides energy and helps the body absorb vitamins
words.example: Unsaturated fats are considered healthier than saturated fats.

words.definitionEn: a type of carbohydrate that the body cannot digest, important for digestive health
words.example: A diet rich in fiber can help prevent constipation.

words.definitionEn: a organic compound that is essential for normal growth and nutrition
words.example: Oranges are a good source of vitamin C.

words.definitionEn: a naturally occurring inorganic substance needed by the body for various functions
words.example: Calcium and iron are important minerals for bone health and blood production.

words.definitionEn: a substance that protects cells from damage caused by free radicals
words.example: Berries are rich in antioxidants that may reduce the risk of chronic diseases.

words.definitionEn: the chemical processes that occur in the body to maintain life, including converting food into energy
words.example: A person's metabolism can affect how quickly they burn calories.

words.definitionEn: the condition of being extremely overweight with a high amount of body fat
words.example: Obesity is a major risk factor for heart disease and diabetes.

words.definitionEn: weighing more than is considered healthy for a particular height
words.example: Being overweight can increase the likelihood of developing health issues.

words.definitionEn: weighing less than is considered healthy
words.example: Underweight individuals may have a weakened immune system.

words.definitionEn: a diet that contains the right proportions of all essential nutrients
words.example: A balanced diet includes fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and lean proteins.

words.definitionEn: relating to the food that a person eats
words.example: Dietary guidelines recommend limiting added sugars and saturated fats.

words.definitionEn: containing a high amount of nutrients relative to its calorie content
words.example: Leafy greens are nutrient-dense foods that provide many vitamins and minerals.

words.definitionEn: food that has been altered from its natural state, often with added preservatives or flavors
words.example: Consuming too much processed food can lead to health problems.

words.definitionEn: produced without the use of synthetic chemicals, such as pesticides or fertilizers
words.example: Organic farming practices are more environmentally sustainable.

words.definitionEn: refers to an organism whose genetic material has been altered using biotechnology
words.example: Genetically modified crops are often engineered to resist pests.

words.definitionEn: a substance added to food to prevent spoilage or extend its shelf life
words.example: Many packaged foods contain artificial preservatives.

words.definitionEn: a substance added to food to improve its flavor, appearance, or texture
words.example: Food additives are regulated to ensure they are safe for consumption.

words.definitionEn: having nutrients added that are not naturally present
words.example: Fortified milk is often enriched with vitamin D.

words.definitionEn: a lack of a specific nutrient that can lead to health problems
words.example: Vitamin D deficiency can cause bone weakness.

words.definitionEn: the amount of food or drink that is taken into the body
words.example: Reducing your salt intake can lower blood pressure.

words.definitionEn: the act of eating or drinking something
words.example: Excessive consumption of sugary drinks is linked to obesity.

words.definitionEn: the amount of food served to one person at one time
words.example: Controlling portion sizes is key to weight management.

words.definitionEn: a standard amount of food used as a reference for dietary guidelines
words.example: A serving of vegetables is about 80 grams.

words.definitionEn: the feeling of needing or wanting to eat
words.example: Chronic hunger can lead to malnutrition.

words.definitionEn: a natural desire to eat
words.example: Regular exercise can help regulate appetite.

words.definitionEn: the feeling of being full after eating
words.example: Foods high in fiber promote satiety and reduce overeating.

words.definitionEn: relating to the process of breaking down food in the body
words.example: Probiotics support digestive health by maintaining gut bacteria.

words.definitionEn: the process by which nutrients from food enter the bloodstream
words.example: Vitamin C enhances the absorption of iron from plant sources.

words.definitionEn: the process of breaking down food into smaller components that can be absorbed
words.example: Chewing thoroughly aids digestion.

words.definitionEn: the practice of cultivating land and raising animals for food production
words.example: Sustainable agriculture aims to minimize environmental impact.

words.definitionEn: the process of growing crops or plants
words.example: The cultivation of rice requires a lot of water.

words.definitionEn: the process of gathering ripe crops from the fields
words.example: The harvest season is a busy time for farmers.

words.definitionEn: animals kept on a farm for food or other products
words.example: Raising livestock contributes to greenhouse gas emissions.

words.definitionEn: domesticated birds such as chickens and turkeys raised for meat or eggs
words.example: Poultry is a lean source of protein.

words.definitionEn: edible marine animals such as fish, shellfish, and crustaceans
words.example: Seafood is rich in omega-3 fatty acids.

words.meaningVi: sữa và các chế phẩm từ sữa
words.definitionEn: food products made from milk, such as cheese, yogurt, and butter
words.example: Dairy products are a good source of calcium.

words.definitionEn: the small hard seeds of cereal plants such as wheat, rice, and corn
words.example: Whole grains are more nutritious than refined grains.

words.definitionEn: a plant whose seeds are eaten as food, such as beans, lentils, and peas
words.example: Legumes are a great source of plant-based protein and fiber.

words.definitionEn: a substance that can cause an allergic reaction
words.example: Peanuts are a common allergen in many processed foods.

words.definitionEn: the inability to properly digest a particular food, leading to discomfort
words.example: Lactose intolerance is common among adults.

words.definitionEn: a chronic condition in which the body cannot regulate blood sugar levels properly
words.example: A diet high in sugar increases the risk of type 2 diabetes.

words.definitionEn: relating to the heart and blood vessels
words.example: A diet rich in fruits and vegetables supports cardiovascular health.

words.definitionEn: able to be maintained over time without depleting natural resources
words.example: Sustainable food production methods are essential for the environment.
